source_row.item_data_json: {"options":{"A":"Use a beta-blocker for a cardiovascular indication when appropriate; cardioselective agents are generally preferred in COPD.","B":"Avoid every beta-blocker in COPD, even with a strong cardiovascular indication and a cardioselective option clearly available.","C":"Start a beta-blocker solely to prevent COPD exacerbations, even when there is no cardiovascular indication for it.","D":"Choose a nonselective beta-blocker routinely because pulmonary beta-2 blockade reduces bronchospasm in COPD patients."}}
source_row.rationale: COPD is not an automatic contraindication to indicated beta-blockade. Current GOLD guidance favors cardioselective agents for established cardiovascular indications and does not support beta-blockers solely to prevent COPD exacerbations.
source_row.source_detail: Comorbid cardiovascular disease/beta-blocker guidance: cardioselective beta-blockers are preferred when a clear cardiovascular indication exists; beta-blockers are not recommended solely to prevent COPD exacerbations without such an indication. GOLD 2026 Report and Pocket Guide; current release rechecked 2026-08-15. Reviewed 2026-08-15.
source_row.stem: A client with COPD has a strong cardiovascular indication for beta-blocker therapy. Which approach aligns with current COPD guidance?
